sections.name: goals
value: The operator can tell a coder from an expert from a human window in the list and the view.

sections.name: non_goals

Recomputing authority from the type: `seat_role_for` and the prime designation are untouched.

value.claim: Migration 0052 adds a nullable `role_type` to `community_pointers`: the pointer of a role document carries its `meta.type`. One row per role, not per holding, so an assign writes nothing new and `Assignment` is unchanged.

The column is a cache of the role document's `meta.type`, refreshed at every point pij writes it: each directory write records its documents' pointers with the type read from the worktree (add, edit, retire, merge, retype), and `pij directory rebuild` recomputes every pointer from the branch head. Only a hand edit of the governance branch can leave it stale, until the next rebuild. `pij directory` reads the documents themselves, so the view is never stale.

Each seat in `pij list --json` (`/v1/seats`) gains `type` (the one type of its open holdings; with none, `prime` for a prime seat, `project-manager` for a `pm` seat, `pa` for a `pa` seat, else null; with two different types, null) and `types` (every distinct type it holds, sorted). Each role row in `pij directory --json` carries `type`. No existing field is removed or renamed. The human `pij list` gains a TYPE column (`-` for null) in both the Rust and the TS renderer, pinned by the shared golden.
A seat whose open holdings carry two different types is a `pij directory` action naming both roles and the release line that splits them.
Every existing permission test passes unchanged: a knowledge-role seat and a coder-role seat show different types and the same worker authority.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Seats are listed by GET /v1/seats (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs) and joined to their seat role by `join_roles` (http/role.rs); community holdings are `community_assignments` (crates/store/src/community.rs). The view is built in community/directory.rs and its actions in community/picture.rs. The OMP and Copilot extensions read `pij list` JSON; new fields are additive. Design change from the first cut: the type rides the role document's pointer (`community_pointers`, written after every directory commit and rebuilt from the branch head) rather than a column on every holding, which would have touched every `Assignment` literal and needed a restamp on each type edit.

value.risk: A stale stamp after a hand edit.
value.mitigation: Stated refresh point: the rebuild. The view reads documents directly.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Cost: migration 0052 is one ALTER at boot. Each directory write already records its pointers; it now also reads each role document it committed once (in-process, no launch). `pij list` adds one indexed store query (open holdings joined to pointers) per call, no file read and no launch. No loop, poll or timer, nothing per seat per tick.
No permission rule changes (PRD 003); no daemon enforcement of a type's rules; no existing JSON field removed or renamed.
Builds nice-19 through `just shared-build`, one at a time.
